events.title: Charlemagne is born, by tradition on this day
events.description: Charlemagne, future King of the Franks and emperor in the West, was traditionally born on 2 April; the year may have been as late as 748. His empire united much of Western Europe for the first time since Rome.
events.html: Charlemagne, future King of the Franks and emperor in the West, was traditionally born on 2 April; the year may have been as late as 748. His empire united much of Western Europe for the first time since Rome.

events.title: Ponce de León sights the coast he names La Florida
events.description: Spanish explorer Juan Ponce de León sighted the Florida coast during the Easter season, Pascua Florida, which gave the land its name. His was the first recorded European landing in what is now the United States.
events.html: Spanish explorer Juan Ponce de León sighted the Florida coast during the Easter season, Pascua Florida, which gave the land its name. His was the first recorded European landing in what is now the United States.

events.title: Bach's cantata Bleib bei uns is first performed in Leipzig
events.description: Johann Sebastian Bach's cantata Bleib bei uns, denn es will Abend werden, BWV 6, written for the Lutheran service on Easter Monday, was first performed in Leipzig. Bach had been cantor there since 1723.
events.html: Johann Sebastian Bach's cantata Bleib bei uns, denn es will Abend werden, BWV 6, written for the Lutheran service on Easter Monday, was first performed in Leipzig. Bach had been cantor there since 1723.

events.title: US Coinage Act creates the dollar and the Mint
events.description: Congress passed the Coinage Act, establishing the United States Mint in Philadelphia and defining the dollar in silver and gold. It laid the foundations of American currency.
events.html: Congress passed the Coinage Act, establishing the United States Mint in Philadelphia and defining the dollar in silver and gold. It laid the foundations of American currency.

events.title: A British fleet defeats the Danish-Norwegian fleet at Copenhagen
events.description: Because Denmark had joined the League of Armed Neutrality, a British fleet under Sir Hyde Parker, with Horatio Nelson leading the attack, engaged the Danish-Norwegian fleet before Copenhagen. After hard fighting a truce was agreed and Denmark left the league.

events.title: Jefferson Davis abandons Richmond as Petersburg falls
events.description: As Union troops broke through the Petersburg lines, Confederate President Jefferson Davis and his government fled Richmond by train. Lee surrendered at Appomattox a week later.
events.html: As Union troops broke through the Petersburg lines, Confederate President Jefferson Davis and his government fled Richmond by train. Lee surrendered at Appomattox a week later.

events.title: Argentina invades the Falkland Islands
events.description: Argentine forces seized the British-held Falklands, which Argentina claims as the Malvinas. Britain sent a naval task force; the ten-week war ended in Argentine surrender and hastened the fall of the junta.
events.html: Argentine forces seized the British-held Falklands, which Argentina claims as the Malvinas. Britain sent a naval task force; the ten-week war ended in Argentine surrender and hastened the fall of the junta.

events.title: Pope John Paul II dies after a 26-year pontificate
events.description: John Paul II, the first non-Italian pope in over four centuries, died in the Vatican. His papacy, one of the longest in history, was closely tied to the fall of communism in his native Poland.
